description: Soybean rust is a foliar disease of soybean caused by the fungus Phakopsora pachyrhizi. It can cause severe yield losses under favorable conditions.
distribution: Originally from Asia; in the U.S., first found in the South in 2004 and spreads northward each growing season.

host_range.other_hosts: Not specified; obligate pathogen surviving only on green host tissue

leaf: Small gray spots on lower leaf surfaces that turn tan or reddish-brown
Pustules (blisters) develop in lesions releasing tan spores
Early symptoms difficult to distinguish from other leaf diseases
pod_stem: Lesions and pustules may appear on pods and stems
symptoms.timing: Most common after flowering, during reproductive stages

conditions_favoring_disease.plant_stage: Reproductive stages, after flowering and pod development

species: Phakopsora meibomiae (mild pathogen, not causing major yield loss)
biology.survival: On living green tissue in southern states and Mexico; spores dispersed by wind northward each season
biology.infection: Lesions develop on lower leaves first; can spread to pods and stems

damage: Yield losses greater than 50% under favorable conditions

cultural_control: Scout lower canopy weekly, especially during wet weather
chemical_control: Use foliar fungicides applied early or immediately after infection
genetic_control: Soybean varieties resistant to rust are under development

notes: Soybean rust requires repeated annual northward spore dispersal to cause epidemics in northern areas
P. pachyrhizi is the aggressive pathogen causing significant yield loss; P. meibomiae is mild and not yet reported in continental U.S.
